problem_text:
A regional courier network is tasked with servicing five distinct distribution hubs, each positioned at specific grid coordinates on a logistics map.  
Hub Alpha: coordinates (124,150)  
Hub Beta: coordinates (161,85)  
Hub Gamma: coordinates (48,62)  
Hub Delta: coordinates (4,187)  
Hub Epsilon: coordinates (69,29)  

The travel distances between hubs, measured in kilometers along available routes, are as follows:  
Alpha to Gamma: 116.3 km  
Alpha to Delta: 125.6 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 132.9 km  
Beta to Gamma: 115.3 km  
Beta to Delta: 187.2 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 107.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 132.5 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 39.1 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 170.8 km  

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct route exists between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta.  
Moreover, due to scheduling and capacity constraints, the final route must incorporate exactly one of the following two critical links: either the connection between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the connection between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a circuit that visits each hub precisely once and returns to the origin hub.
